headline: Oil Prices Plunge 15% on Hopes of US-Iran Peace Deal
summary: Oil prices fell 15% this week, with ICE Brent sliding to $99 per barrel, driven by expectations of U.S.-Iran diplomatic progress despite ongoing attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.
why: Crude oil is a primary global commodity input that affects energy sector equities, transportation costs, and broader inflation expectations, making price swings critical for macroeconomic policy and corporate earnings.
why_moved: Expectations of diplomatic progress between the U.S. and Iran reduced geopolitical risk premiums, leading traders to price in peace and driving a 15% drop in oil prices.
